shipped.title: Settlement reconciliation that measures itself
shipped.thesis: A recon engine that scores its own recall against injected breaks, and refuses to force a match.

shipped.title: Deterministic freshness in shopping-concierge
shipped.thesis: A test that breaks itself 30 days after it is written is not a test. CI now catches it.

shipped.title: Profile README: thesis first, proofs second
shipped.thesis: A bare repo list became a one screen argument, with every claim linked.

shipped.title: Spend policy engine for agent-initiated payments
shipped.thesis: Agents can spend; nothing decides whether they should. Reserve at decision time and a burst cannot overrun the budget.

shipped.title: CI on the trading agent, and the macOS crash it found
shipped.thesis: The suite had never run outside one laptop. On Linux CI it failed 7 tests: the client read the Keychain in its constructor, so every authenticated path crashed with FileNotFoundError security.

shipped.title: Subscription mandate simulator across three rails
shipped.thesis: One scheduler, three rails: 99.48% kept on cards, 60.74% on SEPA, 46.87% on UPI. The rail decides the outcome, not the code.

shipped.title: Rewrite the trading agent README around what it cannot do
shipped.thesis: A rail someone wrote stopped one order and a rule nobody wrote down stopped four. The README now leads with the enforced checks and prints the run record from a committed command.

shipped.title: Money allocation and FX rounding engine
shipped.thesis: One in five payouts did not add up: 621 of 3,000 per share rounded payouts were off, by up to 2 minor units. Largest remainder balanced every one, and all 3,374 cases of an exhaustive sweep.

shipped.title: Keep tokens and the API key out of the SDK log files
shipped.thesis: The SDK's own ERROR handler wrote the bearer token and the API key into logs/ where loglevel() could not reach. A filter on the logger covers the handler the SDK attaches later.

shipped.title: Agent-to-agent credit with exposure limits and netting
shipped.thesis: A $200 cap on gross outflow carried 21.26% of the value, a $200 cap on net debit carried 97.84%, with the same worst case loss. Multilateral netting removed 94.59% of the flow.

shipped.title: Declare the public surface of every public repo, and check it
shipped.thesis: Metadata maintained by hand drifts. 5 of 7 public repos carried no topics and 4 descriptions had grown into feature piles. Desired state now lives in the repo and a committed tool fails on drift.

shipped.title: Idempotency conformance suite for payment APIs
shipped.thesis: A key store is not idempotency. Storing the response after the charge passes 6 of 11 checks and creates 7 charges that should not exist; reserving the key first passes 11 of 11.

shipped.title: Stop publishing the host address and the live book
shipped.thesis: The filed defect was one field in a tracked state file. The scan found 11 host identifiers across 7 tracked files, including two more addresses inside committed broker refusals. The state file is now untracked, fixtures use documentation ranges, and a committed guard fails CI when one grows back.

shipped.title: Sanctions screening that survives a review budget
shipped.thesis: A name screen alerted on 28 of the 36 listed customers in the book and delivered 11, because 130 customers share its top score. Dates, countries and identity numbers pushed 33 through the same 48 reviews.

shipped.title: A reproducible bench and CI for agent-bazaar
shipped.thesis: The mock could not stand in for the model run, it prints four identical rows. Nine scripted hostile proposers give a table that moves, and the first run found 34 price commitments outside the proposer's own limit.

shipped.title: Authorization-rate aware payment routing
shipped.thesis: Routing on the lowest published fee collects 26.9 basis points less in fees and still gives up 4.0 percent of net margin, $1,531 per 1,000 transactions, because the cheapest provider is the worst in 7 of 12 segments. A three-line rule table recovers nearly all of it; learned routing only earns its keep when a provider's approval rate moves, and the all-history posterior then misses the shift while a 300 attempt window tracks it.

shipped.title: Make main the mandate, not the day-0 skeleton
shipped.thesis: The default branch held 2 commits and none of the work: no mandate package, no rails, no run record. Main now carries the 23 commits that built them, merged rather than replayed, so the repo a reader opens is the repo the README describes.

shipped.title: Broker order, fill, and position reconciliation
shipped.thesis: A book reconciled to the broker snapshot alone sits 844 shares and 27.2 lakh rupees away from the exchange tape on a 1,200 order session and reports zero breaks, because it has nothing to compare against. Reconciling the app to the broker flags 206 items at 43 percent precision and still leaves 1,424 shares off. Naming every break from the tape closes the gap to zero, and ranking the 286 breaks by rupee impact puts 87 percent of the exposure inside 60 review tickets against 26 percent in arrival order.

shipped.title: Make the load benchmark a gate, not a table
shipped.thesis: bench/results.md was prose: no machine readable record, no threshold, and nothing failed when a number got worse. One JSON record now feeds the markdown, the gate and CI, and a mutated run returns four named violations.

shipped.title: The three clocks in a chargeback
shipped.thesis: A status tracker recovers 21.3% of the defensible value in a 2,000 dispute book. Three clocks, two zero evidence checks, an evidence gate and a value per minute queue take the same 40 analyst minutes a day to 94.0%, worth $201,675. 55.2% of the recoverable money needs no evidence at all, and the tracker captured 6.4% of it.

shipped.title: Record the data date in the catalog, not the file mtime
shipped.thesis: A fresh clone of the 100 day old catalog reported data as of today, fresh, 0m old, because freshness came from file mtime and git rewrites mtime to the clone time. Neither committed catalog carried a date, so the label measured the checkout, not the data. Both now write _meta.data_as_of at save time and the loader reads it before anything else, with mtime kept as the legacy fallback and the field naming which one it used. Both catalogs were refreshed: 243 synthetic products regenerated byte identical from committed code, and 35 pages re-read on the real store with 8 products kept, 7 seen again and 0 price changes. An August book with a fresh file now reads stale, pinned in tests.

shipped.title: An underwriting model is a probability, or it is a personality test
shipped.thesis: Three models rank the same 1,500 loan holdout identically, AUC 0.7402 and 0.862 accuracy at 0.5 for all three, and disagree by $417,755 of contribution, because one reports a mean PD of 5.99% where 13.73% default and approves 85.9% of the book. Two parameters fitted on 1,500 settled loans cut Brier by 8.8%, take ECE from 0.0951 to 0.0213, and turn a $150,633 loss into $270,379, which is $3,256 above the calibrated baseline. Ranking metrics cannot see the number that prices the loan.
